lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: preparing the night before

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice preparing the night before. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: An adult models a night-before prep routine covering three things: laying out clothes for tomorrow, packing any items needed (school bag, sports gear, etc.), and checking what the first commitment of tomorrow is.
safetyNotes: No overnight or unsupervised nighttime activity is required beyond the learner's normal evening routine.

simulationAlternative.description: If there's no specific real upcoming day to prep for, the learner instead plans the three-item routine in writing for a hypothetical school or activity day described in the lesson, explaining what they would lay out, pack, and check.

materials: learner-local: a bag or container for packed items

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Compare this morning to the bad morning from your warm-up. What specifically was different because of the night-before routine?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Routine completeness: Completes all three parts. | Real-world follow-through: The next morning went smoothly because of the prep. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Run the routine for a night with an unusual next-day event (like an early appointment or something extra to bring) and describe what changed about the routine.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice preparing the night before. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.elapsedWindow: Two short sessions across one day; no continuous monitoring
duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: preparing the night before worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: An adult models a night-before prep routine covering three things: laying out clothes for tomorrow, packing any items needed (school bag, sports gear, etc.), and checking what the first commitment of tomorrow is.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact preparing the night before decision or action.
Model move 2: Before the model, think of one morning that went badly because something wasn't ready the night before.
Model move 3: Watch your adult model the three-item routine (clothes, packed items, first commitment check) for tomorrow, then narrate it back in your own words.
Model check: Routine completeness: Completes all three parts. | Real-world follow-through: The next morning went smoothly because of the prep.

resources.title: preparing the night before action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for preparing the night before.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: preparing the night before coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: An adult models a night-before prep routine covering three things: laying out clothes for tomorrow, packing any items needed (school bag, sports gear, etc.), and checking what the first commitment of tomorrow is.
Coach direction: Before the model, think of one morning that went badly because something wasn't ready the night before.
Learner prompt: Describe that morning.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: preparing the night before complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Watch your adult model the three-item routine (clothes, packed items, first commitment check) for tomorrow, then narrate it back in your own words.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I could name all three parts of the routine after watching.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I could explain why checking tomorrow's first commitment matters, not just packing items.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I helped with at least one part of the modeled routine.

Equal-access rule: If there's no specific real upcoming day to prep for, the learner instead plans the three-item routine in writing for a hypothetical school or activity day described in the lesson, explaining what they would lay out, pack, and check.

resources.title: preparing the night before minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Compare this morning to the bad morning from your warm-up. What specifically was different because of the night-before routine?
Success checks: Routine completeness: Completes all three parts. | Real-world follow-through: The next morning went smoothly because of the prep.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: preparing the night before supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional preparing the night before condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.
Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Routine completeness: Completes all three parts. | Real-world follow-through: The next morning went smoothly because of the prep..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: preparing the night before — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Watch your adult model the three-item routine (clothes, packed items, first commitment check) for tomorrow, then narrate it back in your own words.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
